subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a configurable pre-handshake WebSocket admission layer for strict forwarded-header and `Sec-Fetch-Site` checks, or keep these concerns in the existing post-handshake/browser-origin policy while the related origin-policy work is resolved?
rationale: The code can make the proposed checks opt-in, but deciding whether this new Gateway security layer and its three public settings should become a supported long-term contract is a maintainer product and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Approve the pre-upgrade boundary
options.body: Adopt this layer as Gateway policy after reviewing its final defaults, naming, and raw-wire duplicate-header proof.

options.title: Keep the current boundary
options.body: Decline the new pre-upgrade configuration surface and retain origin enforcement in the existing Gateway admission paths until a narrower owner-approved design exists.

recommendation.title: Approve the pre-upgrade boundary
recommendation.body: Adopt this layer as Gateway policy after reviewing its final defaults, naming, and raw-wire duplicate-header proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged Gateway loopback-origin hardening is the closest current-main implementation history for the browser-admission compatibility boundary.
